title: An unreachable default provider ends every run with 'Retrying this answer in chat-only mode.' and nothing else — the connection error is swallowed, no Retry, no way to Settings, and every indicator stays green
repro: Stack B: Settings › Assistant — default provider is oMLX (http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1, nothing listening). The provider card says 'Active · Qwen3.5-27B-…' with a green dot

First-run view (chat list empty, simulated by routing GET /assistant/chats → []): the welcome screen offers four sample prompts under a green pill 'Qwen3.5-27B-…', with no hint that a local model server must be running and no provider setup CTA; clicking a suggestion leads to the same dead end
Assistant › New, model pill → Provider oMLX, type 'hello', Enter
Wait 5 s, then 60 s. Also repeat in the Designer dock (Cmd+I) on Schem and on PCB
Check GET /api/modules/tasks/tasks/<taskId> and GET /chats/<id>/messages
expected: Within a few seconds a clear error in the message bubble: 'Can't reach oMLX at http://127.0.0.1:8000 — is the server running?', with Retry and an 'Open provider settings' action. The provider status dot/pill turns red or amber.
actual: After ~1.1 s the bubble shows only the italic line 'Provider failed while tools were enabled. Retrying this answer in chat-only mode.' Nothing else ever appears — no answer, no error, no Retry, no link to Settings. The task is status 'completed' with error null (created 18:56:35.723, completed 18:56:35.750), and the persisted message content is just that warning. The chat-only retry fails too (ECONNREFUSED), but its run.failed event is not captured. The run therefore counts as answered and the empty_response Retry path never fires. The same happens in the dock on Schem and PCB (each send adds another 'Retrying…' bubble). Every health indicator stays green throughout: the Settings card shows 'Active' (#6fbf7a, --status-success), the header pill dot is emerald #00bc7d, the sidebar footer dot is #6fbf7a and the chat row dot is green. The pill's model list shows 4 cached oMLX models, so nothing hints that the server is down.

network: message a91d2c4b content: '_Provider failed while tools were enabled. Retrying this answer in chat-only mode._'

codeRefs.note: on failedEvent writes the 'Retrying…' warning, then runs the chat-only retry without capturing its own run.failed
answeredOrToolWork() is true because the warning text is non-blank → no empty_response, task completes as success
run.failed is only forwarded as an ai event; never turns the task into failed
'Active ·' label depends only on enabled plus a model, not on reachability
green 'Tools + streaming OK' comes from a stale capabilities probe and never reflects the current connection (raw bg-emerald-500)

suggestedFix: In run-service.ts capture run.failed from the chat-only retry as well. If the retry also fails, or the first failure is a transport error (ECONNREFUSED/ENOTFOUND/timeout), for which a tools-off retry is pointless, fail the task with {type:'provider', message:'Can't reach <label> at <baseUrl>'} and replace the 'Retrying…' text. In the frontend, render failed runs with Retry plus an 'Open provider settings' button (wire onOpenSettings, see Q8-008). Show provider reachability, e.g. the 5 s probe in assistant-service.ts:324, as an amber/red pill dot instead of always-green.

title: A hung local provider blocks the chat for good: provider calls have no timeout, a second send orphans the running run (it loses its Stop), and later messages sit behind it as a fake 'Working…'
repro: Stack B, default provider oMLX at 127.0.0.1:8000. Simulate a hung local server, e.g. LM Studio still loading a model: a TCP listener on :8000 that accepts and never replies (QA used f2c/blackhole.py)
QA-f2c-board → Cmd+I dock → type 'hello hung provider' → Enter: 'Working… Stop' appears (OK)
Reload the page and reopen Designer → dock: the bubble shows 'Working… Stop' again, but the composer now shows an enabled Send button instead of 'Stop generating'
Type 'second while running' → Enter
Open in Assistant view; press Stop on the visible run; send 'third message'
expected: Provider requests time out (e.g. 60–120 s for first byte) with a clear error. While a run is in flight the composer offers Stop, not a second Send. If a message is queued it reads 'Queued — waiting for the previous answer', and every in-flight run keeps a Stop control.
actual: No timeout: the first task stayed 'streaming' for 6 min 51 s (19:04:34 → 19:11:25) and ended only because the fake server closed the socket. It then 'completed' with the misleading 'Retrying … chat-only mode' text (see F2C-001). After the reload, Send was enabled mid-run. The second send was accepted (201) and its task went to status 'waiting' (scope-serialised behind the hung task). The dock/space track one run per chat, so the new run replaced the old one: the hung run's bubble became an empty 'Assistant' header with no Stop, while the waiting run showed a spinner 'Working…'. 'waiting' is not handled in taskStage and falls through to 'running'. Stop cancels only the waiting task. The hung task has no control anywhere in the dock or the Assistant space, and every further message in that chat ('third message') again waits behind it, shown as 'Working…'. The only escapes are waiting it out or starting a new chat.

codeRefs.note: taskStage has no 'waiting' case → default 'running' → 'Working…' (same in Space.tsx:451)
restored run bound per chat; a new submit overwrites the chat's single activeRun, orphaning the in-flight one
scope lock per chatId: later tasks wait for the hung one indefinitely
only the capability probe has AbortSignal.timeout; the chat completion call has none

suggestedFix: Give provider chat calls a timeout: AbortSignal.any([taskSignal, AbortSignal.timeout(n)]) around first byte plus an idle-stream timeout, and fail the task with a readable 'Provider did not respond in N s' error. After a restore, set the composer to busy/Stop whenever the chat has an in-flight task (restoreActiveTask should set the composer's run, not only the bubble's), or keep a list of runs per chat. Map 'waiting'/'queued' to 'Queued behind the previous answer…' with its own Cancel.

title: After 'Open in Assistant view', every chat-list refresh snaps the Assistant space back to that chat — sending in a New chat or pressing Stop elsewhere jumps you away mid-conversation
repro: Designer › QA-f2c-board › dock (Cmd+I) › 'Open in Assistant view' (opens 'QA-f2c-board chat')
In the Assistant space click 'New', type 'jump test', press Enter
Within 0.5 s read the thread header
Also: in another chat press Stop / 'Stop generating' on a running answer
expected: The space stays on the chat you are using. 'Open in Assistant view' selects its chat once.
actual: Within 0.5 s of sending, the header reads 'QA-f2c-board chat' again. The new chat (with the 'jump test' message and its answer) is deselected in the list, so the reply lands in a chat you are not looking at. Pressing 'Stop generating' in a new chat does the same: the run is cancelled, then the view jumps. The jump repeats on every refresh (send, run end, cancel) until you leave the Assistant space through the rail. After re-entering through the rail it does not happen.

codeRefs.note: refreshChats: `next = routeChat ?? current` — the route param chatId wins over the user's current selection on every refresh
routeChatId = params?.chatId stays set for the whole visit

suggestedFix: In Space.tsx apply routeChatId once: keep a ref of the last handled route chatId and select it only when it changes, e.g. in a useEffect on routeChatId. In refreshChats prefer `current` when it still exists. Alternatively clear the route param with navigation-store replace after the first selection.

title: Picking a cloud provider with no API key: the pill keeps the previous provider's model, the footer stays green, and the send error 'API key required for provider: OpenAI' offers no way to add a key
repro: Stack B (no keys). Assistant › chat on oMLX › model pill → Provider 'OpenAI'
Observe the Model field, pill dot and sidebar footer
Close the popover, type 'hello openai', Enter; press Enter again (retry)
Repeat in the Designer dock (Cmd+I)
expected: Unconfigured providers are marked in the Provider select ('OpenAI — needs API key') or disabled. Selecting one shows an inline 'Add API key' action. The model resets to that provider's default. A send error gives a one-click route to the provider settings.
actual: The Provider select lists OpenAI with no hint. In the Assistant space the Model field becomes a free-text box still holding the oMLX model 'Qwen3.5-27B-Claude-4.6-Opus-Distilled-MLX-4bit' (the dock correctly switches to gpt-4o-mini, so the two surfaces disagree). The pill dot turns red (#fb2c36, raw red-500, tooltip-only 'API key required'), but the sidebar footer still shows a green dot with 'Qwen3.5-27B-… · OpenAI'. On send, POST /messages → 400 and a red banner 'API key required for provider: OpenAI' (Dismiss only) appears at the top of the thread, not next to the composer. There is no 'Add key'/'Open settings' link, the pill's 'Configure providers' is dead (Q8-008), and Enter just repeats the 400. The typed text stays in the composer (good) but is lost on reload. In a chat with history (light, 1100×720, 'QA-f2c-board chat') the same banner renders at top=-592px, above the scrolled thread. Nothing visible changes on send except the text staying in the composer (same placement root as Q8-017).

codeRefs.note: only the pill dot knows about requiresApiKey; the provider <select> options don't
sidebar footer dot is always green regardless of provider state

suggestedFix: In ModelSelectorPill, suffix options with '— needs API key' (or disable them) using the same requiresApiKey && !hasApiKey check. On provider change in Space, reset the model to provider.defaultModel, as the dock does. Map the 400 'API key required' error to an inline composer notice with an 'Add API key' button that opens Settings › Assistant with that provider expanded. Drive the footer dot from the same status function as the pill.

title: When the OS theme changes while the schematic is open (Appearance = System, the default), the canvas keeps the previous palette: parts go invisible on light, or a glaring white sheet appears in dark
repro: Settings › General › Appearance = System (the default when no preference is stored)
Open QA-f2c-board › Schem (parts + one wire), Fit schematic
Change the OS appearance (QA: page.emulateMedia({colorScheme:'light'}) then 'dark'), do not touch the canvas
Pixel-probe canvas bg, wire, part body and outline. Compare with a fresh reload in the same theme
expected: The whole schematic re-themes with the shell, identical to a fresh load in that theme (light: bg #f0f4fb, wire #3e506b, body #dbdbd9, outline #020616).
actual: Dark → light (live): the background switches to #f0f4fb, but parts and wires keep the dark palette. Body is #030303 (black box), outlines #d9dbde (1.26:1 on the bg, so R1/C1/J1 are practically invisible), wire #a6b2c1 (1.95:1). Light → dark (live): the canvas turns into a bright #f5f5f0 sheet with light-palette parts inside the dark shell (17:1 against the surrounding chrome). The zoom cluster also stays in the old style. The stale palette stays until something re-renders the scene; any click on the canvas fixes it. Switching through Settings › Light/Dark is fine, because the designer unmounts while Settings is open. Library list/detail, portalled menus and Docs re-theme correctly on the same live switch. The PCB canvas is identical in both themes anyway (Q4-038).

codeRefs.note: system-change path calls setMode(nextMode); applyThemeClass runs later in a useEffect, so during that render <html data-color-mode> still holds the old mode
themeMode='auto' reads document.documentElement.dataset.colorMode at render time → resolves the stale mode
EdaCanvas gets backgroundColor from useTheme() but no themeMode prop, so bg and palette come from different sources

suggestedFix: In SchematicCanvas (and PcbCanvas) pass themeMode={mode} from useTheme() to <EdaCanvas>, so the canvas palette follows React state instead of the DOM attribute. Additionally, call applyThemeClass(nextMode) synchronously inside the subscribeToSystemTheme callback in ThemeProvider.tsx before setMode, so every consumer that reads the <html> attribute sees the new mode on the same render.

title: If the Library list request fails, the table becomes a bare red 'HTTP 500' line with '0 of 76' — no message, no Retry. It recovers only after you change the search or a facet
repro: Stack B. route '**/api/modules/library/components?**' → 500 problem+json (detail requests /components/:id/detail are not matched)
Open Library from Home (first open)
Type 'ne5' in search; clear it; tick Family › ic
unroute; wait 3 s; then toggle the facet again
expected: An inline error state in the table area: 'Couldn't load components' with the server's reason and a Retry button, plus a neutral count (not '0 of 76'). Recovery through Retry, or automatically on focus/refresh.
actual: First open: the header says '76 parts · 3 sources' (from /facets), the count row says '0 of 76', and under it is a single 12px red line 'HTTP 500' (raw status, no explanation). The preview pane says 'Select a part to preview'. Search 'ne5' gives '1 part · 1 source' / '0 of 1' / 'HTTP 500'. The facet 'ic' gives '7 parts · 2 sources' / '0 of 7' / 'HTTP 500'. The facet rail and chips keep working, so the UI looks like the filter matched nothing. After unroute nothing refetches: the error stays until the query or a facet changes, or you leave Library and come back. The same bare error line is the delete/ZIP-import failure surface (K08/Q6-003), so this confirms K08 for the list-load path too.

codeRefs.note: throws `HTTP ${status}` and ignores the problem+json title/detail
error rendered as a bare text-status-danger line, no retry/dismiss
counts come from facets.total even when the list failed → '0 of 76'

suggestedFix: In Space.tsx keep a `reloadNonce` in the searchUrl effect deps and render the error as a kit empty-state: icon, 'Couldn't load components', the problem+json title/detail when present, and a Retry button that bumps the nonce. Hide the 'N of M' count while error is set. Reuse the same component for the delete/import failures (K08).

title: A failed /facets request is silent: the filter rail disappears and the header claims '60 parts · 0 sources' / '60 of 60' while the library has 76 parts in 3 sources
repro: Stack B. route '**/api/modules/library/facets**' → 500
Home → Library
Read the header, count row and left rail
unroute; wait; type and delete a character in search
expected: The facet rail shows 'Filters unavailable — Retry' and the header keeps a truthful count, or none, instead of inventing one from the truncated list.
actual: The left rail is an empty 220px column with no message. The header reads '60 parts · 0 sources' and the count row '60 of 60', although the library has 76 parts in 3 sources (the list is capped at 60, Q6-002). This tells the user the list is complete while 16 parts are unreachable. The only trace is a console 500. After unroute nothing refetches until the search text changes (then '76 parts · 3 sources', rail back).

codeRefs.note: `const { facets } = useLibraryFacets(...)` drops the hook's `error`
error captured but never surfaced
totalCount falls back to components.length (the 60-item page) and sourceCount to 0

suggestedFix: Use `facets.error` in Space.tsx: render an inline 'Filters unavailable · Retry' row in the rail (the hook needs a refetch), and when facets failed show only '60 shown' with no total or source count.

title: If the comment list fails to load, every pin silently disappears; you can still post, and the new comment shows as '1' — no error, no Retry
repro: QA-f2c-board has 31 schematic threads
route '**/designs/*/comments?**' → 500 (only the list GET, not thread detail/commands)
Home → Designer (design opens on Schem), Fit schematic
Comment tool → click canvas → 'QA-f2c posted while list failed' → Cmd+Enter
unroute; wait 3 s; then Schem → PCB → Schem
expected: A visible 'Comments couldn't load · Retry' notice, e.g. a chip on the Comment toolbar button or a banner over the canvas. Posting is disabled, or clearly flagged, while the list is unknown. Pin numbers stay stable.
actual: The canvas shows 0 pins, with no banner, toast or indicator. The only trace is a console 500. The design looks as if it had no comments. The Comment tool still works, and the new thread is created (POST 200) and drawn as pin '1'; once the list loads it becomes '32', so the numbers aren't stable identifiers. After unroute nothing refetches (still 1 pin after 3 s). The 31 threads come back only after switching view tabs or reopening the design. useDesignerComments sets `error`, but nothing renders it.

codeRefs.note: catch → setError only; `error` is never consumed by Space.tsx:361
pin number = array index + 1 → renumbers when the list is partial

suggestedFix: Render comments.error in the designer: e.g. a small danger chip on the Comment toolbar button plus a dismissible canvas banner 'Couldn't load comments · Retry' that calls comments.refresh(). Also refetch on window focus/online. Number pins by a persisted per-design sequence (or createdAt order from the server) rather than the local array index.

title: Long comment threads open at the oldest message, and a reply you post lands ~2300 px below the fold with no scroll or confirmation
repro: QA-f2c-board › Schem: thread #1 has a 2000-char first message, a 300-char URL reply and 25 short replies
Click pin 1
Scroll the thread to the top, type 'QA-f2c newest reply 26' in 'Reply to thread…', Cmd+Enter
expected: The thread opens scrolled to the newest message (or a 'N earlier messages' collapse), and posting a reply scrolls it into view. Short replies are compact, without a permanent reaction chip on each one.
actual: The popup (320×570px, max-h 70%) opens with scrollTop 0 on the 2000-char opening message; the 25 replies are below (scrollHeight 2689 vs 429 visible). After posting, the composer clears but scrollTop stays 0. The new reply's top is at y=3051 while the list's visible range is 348–777, so there's no visible sign the reply posted. Each one-line reply takes ~70px (author row, text, and an always-visible 👍 reaction chip), so 25 replies make ~1800px of scroll. The header shows only 'Local · 3m', with no message count. Long text and the unbroken 300-char URL wrap correctly (no horizontal overflow), and the wheel scrolls the popup, not the canvas (good).

codeRefs.note: overflow-y-auto message list; no scroll-to-bottom on open or after addMessage
popup max-h-[70%] w-80

suggestedFix: In CommentThreadPopup, keep a ref on the message list and scroll it to the bottom (or to the first unread) when the thread id changes and after a successful addMessage. Show reaction chips only when a message has reactions, with the add-reaction button on hover. Group consecutive messages from the same author, and add 'N replies' to the header.

title: With many threads, comment pins pile up unreadably (10 overlapping pins, numbers hidden), pins at the right edge are half-clipped instead of becoming off-screen chips, and Fit ignores comments
repro: QA-f2c-board › Schem with 31 threads (10 anchored within ±3 mm of U1, the rest spread over ±45 × ±30 mm)
Fit schematic (zoom 20%)
Inspect the pin cluster on U1 and the right canvas edge
expected: Overlapping pins collapse into a count bubble ('10') that expands or zooms on click, or at least stay individually readable. Pins whose anchors are near an edge are fully drawn or turned into edge chips like the left side. Fit can include comment anchors, or offers a 'Fit comments' option.
actual: Threads 2–10 and 12 render as a 60×80px stack over U1's pins and body. Numbers 3, 4, 5 and 7 are fully covered and 6/9 half-covered, so only the topmost thread is clickable without zooming in, and the pins also cover the U1 pin endpoints (clicking there opens a comment instead of starting a wire). On the right edge pins 28 (x 1119–1147) and 11 (1115–1143) are cut in half by the canvas edge at x=1139. On the left edge, threads 19 and 30 correctly turn into round off-screen chips, so the two sides behave differently. Fit schematic frames only the parts, which leaves 2 threads off-screen. Pins have no accessible name beyond the number (Q5-031). Dragging a pin works and persists (thread revision 2, new anchor). At 1100×720 (light), after the window shrinks, the U1 cluster's off-screen chips pile into one vertical stack of overlapping circles at the left edge (30, 24, 9, 29 and more hidden underneath). Pins 10, 12 and 4 are half-cut at the left edge and pin 23 at the right edge, and the chips never de-overlap.

codeRefs.note: layer is overflow-hidden; the on-screen test uses the anchor point, not the pin's 28px box → half-clipped pins
every thread rendered as an individual pin, no clustering

suggestedFix: In CanvasCommentLayer, treat anchors within ~pin width of an edge as off-screen, so they become edge chips (inset by the pin size). Cluster pins whose screen positions fall within ~20px into one count bubble that zooms or fans out on click. Add a comments list (threads panel or a menu on the Comment button) so every thread is reachable without hunting on the canvas.

title: Dock header row overflows at the default dock width: with a local model name the tools badge is cut off at the window edge and the 'just now' timestamp is pushed out of view
repro: QA-f2c-board › Cmd+I (dock default width ~300px)
Chat on provider oMLX (model 'Qwen3.5-27B-Claude-4.6-Opus-Distilled-MLX-4bit')
Look at the row under the chat selector: model pill · tools badge · timestamp
expected: The pill truncates, or the row wraps, so the tools badge and timestamp stay inside the dock.
actual: The pill (already truncated to 22 chars plus 'STRICT') and the shrink-0 badge/timestamp don't fit in the ~276px row. At 1440×900 the tools badge spans x 1405.9–1447.9 in a 1440px window, so its right half and the whole timestamp are clipped by the window edge. At 1100×720 it spans 1065.9–1107.9 in a 1100px window. The dock container has no overflow handling (the parent is overflow:visible), so the content is simply cut at the viewport edge. With the short 'gpt-4o-mini' model the row fits, so it depends on the model name.

codeRefs.note: `mt-2 flex items-center gap-2` row: pill has no min-w-0/flex-shrink, badge and timestamp are shrink-0
shortModel truncates by character count (22) rather than CSS width

suggestedFix: Give the pill wrapper `min-w-0 flex-1` and the model label `truncate` (CSS ellipsis instead of the 22-char slice). Alternatively move the timestamp to the chat selector row, or hide it below ~320px dock width.

title: 'New' chat reuses the last-viewed chat's provider/model and ignores Settings › Assistant › Default provider
repro: Settings › Assistant: Default provider = oMLX
Assistant space: open chat 'edge unbound v2' (OpenCode Zen)
Click 'New'
expected: A new chat starts on the configured default provider/model (oMLX / Qwen…), or the pill clearly says it is carrying over the previous chat's model.
actual: The new chat's pill reads 'big-pickle · Strict' (OpenCode Zen, and not even that chat's saved model 'deepseek-v4-flash-free', see Q8-001), and the first send creates the chat on that provider. The Settings default applies only when no chat was selected. The same happens after a reload: the auto-selected most-recent chat decides the provider of the next New chat.

codeRefs.note: createChat posts `providerId || settings.defaultProviderId`; providerId still holds the previously selected chat's provider
selecting a chat sets providerId; 'New' never resets it

suggestedFix: When 'New' is clicked (the handler that clears selection before createChat), reset providerId/model to settings.defaultProviderId and that provider's defaultModel. Or make 'use the last model' an explicit option and label the Settings field accordingly.
